
`pksR` reads the district (Kreis) tables of the German Police Crime Statistics (*Polizeiliche Kriminalstatistik*, PKS) of the Bundeskriminalamt (BKA) from versioned data releases. This vignette shows the main functions and describes the columns. The examples that need the internet are shown but not run here; the others use `pks_example()`, a small panel that ships with the package.

```{r}
library(pksR)
```

## Getting data

`pks_get()` downloads the years you ask for from the latest data release, checks every file against its SHA-256 checksum and keeps it in a local cache:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Total offences, harmonized to the latest boundary (the default)
total <- pks_get(offence = "total")

# Offences by key, short name or label, in English or German
burglary <- pks_get(offence = c("residential_burglary", "einbruch"), lang = "en")

# Two years as published by the BKA, all offence keys
published <- pks_get(years = 2024:2025, harmonize_to = NULL)

# A fixed data release, for reproducible work
d <- pks_get(years = 2015:2025, version = "2026.1")
```

The three choices of `harmonize_to`:

| `harmonize_to` | Result |
|---|---|
| `"latest"` (default) | Harmonized to the boundary of the release, read as released |
| a year, e.g. `2016` | The data as published, harmonized to that year's boundary in your session (forward only) |
| `NULL` | As published: each year with the districts of its own boundary |

See `vignette("harmonization")` for the methods and their assumptions.

## Choosing offences

`offence` takes, for each element, an offence key (`"435*00"`), a short name (`"residential_burglary"`, or the German `"wohnungseinbruch"`), a full label in either language, or a part of a label (`"einbruch"` selects both burglary keys and says so). Capitals, spaces and umlauts do not matter, and an exact key, name or label wins over a part. `pks_offences()` lists all keys with their names; the names are drafts until the maintainer has reviewed them.

## Languages

Messages and offence labels come in English or German: `options(pksR.lang = "de")`, or `lang = "de"` in `pks_get()` and `pks_offences()`. Without either, the language of the R session decides. A German version of this vignette is `vignette("pksR-de")`.

## The example panel

```{r}
d <- pks_example()
d[, c("year", "ags", "region_name", "offence_key", "cases", "hz", "harmonized")]
```

Every object carries its provenance as attributes:

```{r}
attributes(d)[c("data_version", "boundary_year", "weights")]
```

For data from `pks_get()`, `data_version` is the release version, `retrieved_at` the time of download and `source_urls` the release files the data came from.

## Columns

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| `year` | Reporting year |
| `ags` | District code (Kreisschlüssel), 5 digits with leading zero, e.g. `"02000"` for Hamburg |
| `region_name` | District name as published, or the name at the target boundary for changed districts |
| `offence_key` | Offence key (Straftatenschlüssel); in harmonized data the harmonized key, see `pks_offences()` |
| `offence_key_published` | Harmonized data only: the key as published, or `"KEY minus KEY"` for computed keys |
| `offence_label` | German label as published |
| `cases` | Recorded cases (published; `NA` in the PDF years 2003 to 2012) |
| `attempts` | Attempted cases |
| `hz` | Häufigkeitszahl: cases per 100,000 inhabitants |
| `cleared` | Cleared cases |
| `clearance_rate` | Aufklärungsquote in percent (0 where cases are 0, as in the BKA tables) |
| `suspects` | Suspects (persons; not additive over offence keys) |
| `cases_derived`, `cleared_derived` | PDF years only: `hz * population / 1e5`, because those tables print rates and population but no counts |
| `population` | Published population (PDF years and 2020) |
| `derived_population` | `cases / hz * 1e5`, derived from the published rate; one value per district and year |
| `source_format`, `source_file` | Format and file of the BKA source |
| `boundary_year` | Territorial boundary (Gebietsstand) of the row |
| `harmonized` | `TRUE` if the district was changed by harmonization |
| `weight_type` | `none`, `population` or `area` |
| `estimated` | `TRUE` for shares of split districts and for derived counts (PDF years) |

Counts in harmonized data are doubles: a split district passes fractions of its cases to its successors, and rounding them would change the national totals.

## Offence keys and breaks

```{r}
pks_offences("theft", lang = "en")[, c("offence_key", "name", "label")]
```

The district tables contain only a selected set of offence keys, and keys change over time. Before reading a time series, check the known methodological breaks:

```{r}
b <- pks_breaks()
b[b$comparable == "no", c("first_year", "offence_key", "type")]
```

## Rates, checks and citation

After filtering or harmonizing, recompute rates from the counts and run the checks:

```{r}
r <- pks_rates(d, per = 1000)
head(r[, c("year", "ags", "offence_key", "cases", "rate")])
pks_validate(d)
```

Work with these data should cite the package, the data release and the sources. `pks_cite()` returns all five entries, including the licence of the BKA data (Datenlizenz Deutschland, Namensnennung, Version 2.0):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pks_cite()
```

## Cache

Downloads are kept below `tools::R_user_dir("pksR", "cache")`, one folder per data version. A release never changes, so a cached file is used until its checksum fails.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pks_cache_info()
pks_cache_clear(version = "2026.1")
```
